subproblem.title: Uniform bounds on compact sets from finite total masses and eventual ball bounds
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let ν_i (i ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^P (= Euclid P) with ν_i(ℝ^P) < ∞ for every i. Assume that for every R > 0 there is B ∈ [0,∞] with B < ∞ such that ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all sufficiently large i (eventually along atTop). Then sup_i ν_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ i, ν i univ < ∞) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ B : ℝ≥0∞, B < ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ν i (closedBall 0 R) ≤ B) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ⨆ i, ν i K < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (sup_i ν_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K). There the early indices are bounded by ν_i(K) ≤ c_i·Hⁿ(M), which equals ν_i(ℝ^P), and the late indices by ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ 2V(R); here these two inputs are the two hypotheses.
1. (Enclosing ball.) K is compact, hence bounded, so K ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R := max(R₀, 1). Then R ≥ 1 > 0 and K ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) ⊆ B̄_R(0).
2. (Late indices.) By the hypothesis applied to this R there are B < ∞ and N ∈ ℕ with ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all i ≥ N (eventually_atTop).
3. (Early indices.) Let S := Σ_{j=0}^{N−1} ν_j(ℝ^P). Each summand is finite by hypothesis, so S < ∞ (ENNReal.sum_lt_top).
4. (Pointwise bound.) Let i ∈ ℕ. If i ≥ N, then ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B by monotonicity of ν_i and steps 1–2. If i < N, then ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(ℝ^P) ≤ S by monotonicity of ν_i and because ν_i(ℝ^P) is one of the summands of S, all of which are ≥ 0 (Finset.single_le_sum with i ∈ {0, …, N−1}). In both cases ν_i(K) ≤ max(B, S).
5. (Conclusion.) Hence sup_i ν_i(K) ≤ max(B, S) (iSup_le), and max(B, S) < ∞ because B < ∞ and S < ∞ (max_lt). ∎
proof_key_steps: K compact ⇒ K ⊆ B̄_R(0) with R := max(R₀, 1) > 0.
The hypothesis gives B < ∞ and N with ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all i ≥ N.
For i < N, ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(ℝ^P) ≤ Σ_{j<N} ν_j(ℝ^P) < ∞.
sup_i ν_i(K) ≤ max(B, Σ_{j<N} ν_j(ℝ^P)) < ∞.

audit.reason: A containing ball controls the tail; the finite sum of initial total masses controls the remaining indices. Their finite maximum bounds the exact supremum in the conclusion.

subproblem.title: Operator norm of an n-covector is at most Pⁿ times its Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear map α : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n). Let ‖α‖ be its operator norm (the norm of continuous alternating maps, ‖α‖ = sup{|α(v_0,…,v_{n−1})| : ‖v_k‖ ≤ 1}) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard orthonormal basis. Then ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·|α|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖α‖ ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0, fact (F1), of the parent proof (blow-ups at a good point); the parent uses it for (F2) in step 1 and for ‖ω(y)‖_op ≤ Pⁿ|ω(y)| ≤ Pⁿ in step 10.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i for i ∈ Fin P; for J : Fin n → Fin P write e∘J for the n-tuple (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}).
1. (Coefficient bound.) For every J : Fin n → Fin P we have |α(e∘J)| ≤ |α|.
 (a) If J is not injective, choose i ≠ j with J(i) = J(j). Then the tuple e∘J has equal entries in the positions i ≠ j, so α(e∘J) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq), and 0 ≤ |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg).
 (b) If J is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort J; it is a permutation of Fin n with J∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). J∘σ is injective and monotone, hence strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective). Since α is alternating, α((e∘J)∘σ) = sign(σ)·α(e∘J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap with the tuple e∘J passed explicitly), and sign(σ) = ±1 (Int.units_eq_one_or), so |α(e∘J)| = |α(e∘I)| with I := J∘σ strictly increasing. Now α(e∘I)² is one of the summands in Σ_{I'} (if I' strictly increasing then α(e∘I')² else 0), all summands being ≥ 0, so α(e∘I)² ≤ that sum (Finset.single_le_sum) and therefore |α(e∘I)| ≤ √(sum) = |α| (Real.abs_le_sqrt).
2. (Multilinear expansion.) Let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and write v_k(i) for the i-th coordinate of v_k. Each v_k = Σ_{i ∈ Fin P} v_k(i)·e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for basisFun). By multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum), α(v) = Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} α((v_k(J(k))·e_{J(k)})_k), and pulling out the scalars (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ for α.toContinuousMultilinearMap) α((v_k(J(k))·e_{J(k)})_k) = (Π_k v_k(J(k)))·α(e∘J).
3. (Estimate.) |v_k(i)| ≤ ‖v_k‖ for every coordinate (PiLp.norm_apply_le). By the triangle inequality (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs), |Π_k v_k(J(k))| = Π_k |v_k(J(k))| ≤ Π_k ‖v_k‖ (Finset.abs_prod, Finset.prod_le_prod₀) and step 1, |α(v)| ≤ Σ_J (Π_k ‖v_k‖)·|α| = #(Fin n → Fin P)·|α|·Π_k ‖v_k‖ = P^n·|α|·Π_k ‖v_k‖ (Finset.sum_const, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin).
4. (Conclusion.) Since P^n·|α| ≥ 0 and |α(v)| ≤ (P^n·|α|)·Π_k ‖v_k‖ for all v, the operator-norm bound ContinuousAlternatingMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·|α|. The degenerate cases need no separate treatment: for n = 0 there is exactly one J (the empty map, strictly increasing) and the estimate reads |α()| ≤ |α|; for P = 0 < n there is no J, the sum is empty and α(v) = 0. ∎
Lean remarks (checked against the pinned Mathlib 25730c7c): ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_perm does not exist, so use α.toAlternatingMap.map_perm with the tuple given explicitly; Finset.prod_le_prod needs MulLeftMono and does not apply on ℝ, so use Finset.prod_le_prod₀; push_neg is deprecated in favour of push Not.
proof_key_steps: Each basis coefficient α(e_{J(0)},…,e_{J(n−1)}) has absolute value ≤ |α|: it is 0 if J is not injective, and ± a strictly increasing coefficient otherwise (sort J, alternating sign).
Expand α(v) multilinearly in the standard basis: α(v) = Σ_J (Π_k v_k(J(k)))·α(e∘J).
Bound |v_k(i)| ≤ ‖v_k‖ and count the P^n terms: |α(v)| ≤ P^n|α|Π_k‖v_k‖.
Conclude ‖α‖ ≤ P^n|α| by ContinuousAlternatingMap.opNorm_le_bound.

audit.reason: Sorting index tuples bounds every basis coefficient. Multilinear expansion, coordinate bounds and counting P^n terms prove the exact operator-norm estimate, including the degenerate dimensions.

subproblem.title: A limsup bound through closed thickenings of a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, a : ℕ → [0,∞], ν_k (k ∈ ℕ) and ν measures on ℝ^P, c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞, and K ⊆ ℝ^P compact. Assume ν(K') < ∞ and limsup_k ν_k(K') ≤ ν(K') for every compact K' ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume also that for every r > 0 there is v : ℕ → [0,∞] with v_k → 0 and a_k ≤ c·ν_k(cthickening r K) + v_k for all k, where cthickening r K is the closed r-thickening of K. Then limsup_k a_k ≤ c·ν(K).

subproblem.title: Transfer of right-limits at 0 to a positive null sequence, times a finite constant
subproblem.statement: Let f, h : ℝ → [0,∞], let C ∈ [0,∞] with C ≠ ∞, and let s : ℕ → ℝ satisfy s_i > 0 for every i and s_i → 0 as i → ∞. Then (i) if limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1 (limsup along 𝓝[>] 0), then limsup_{i→∞} C·f(s_i) ≤ C; and (ii) if h(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0), then C·h(s_i) → 0 as i → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (f h : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (C : ℝ≥0∞) (s : ℕ → ℝ), C ≠ ∞ → (∀ i, 0 < s i) → Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 0) → (limsup f (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ 1 → limsup (fun i => C * f (s i)) atTop ≤ C) ∧ (Tendsto h (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun i => C * h (s i)) atTop (𝓝 0))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the limit arguments of steps 4 and 7 of the parent proof (ε_i(R) = ω_nRⁿ·o(λ_iR)/(ω_n(λ_iR)ⁿ) → 0, and limsup_k λ_{φ(k)}^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{λ_{φ(k)}R}(a)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ·limsup_{r↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ); i.e. composition with λ_iR → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0 and multiplication by the finite constant V(R) = ω_nRⁿ), stated for an arbitrary positive null sequence s and an arbitrary finite constant C.
1. (s tends to 0 from the right.) Since s_i → 0 and s_i ∈ (0, ∞) for every i, s tends to 0 within (0, ∞), i.e. s → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Consequently, if a property Q(r) holds for all r in some member of 𝓝[>] 0, then Q(s_i) holds for all sufficiently large i.
2. (Pulling out the constant in (i).) Assume limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1. Since C ≠ ∞, limsup_i C·f(s_i) = C·limsup_i f(s_i) (ENNReal.limsup_const_mul_of_ne_top, valid for every filter; ENNReal.limsup_const_mul would instead require a countable-intersection filter). Hence it suffices to show L := limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ 1, because then limsup_i C·f(s_i) = C·L ≤ C·1 = C (monotonicity of multiplication in [0,∞]).
3. (L ≤ 1.) Let c ∈ [0,∞] with c > 1. Then limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1 < c, so f(r) < c for all r in some member of 𝓝[>] 0 (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt; its boundedness side condition holds automatically in the complete lattice [0,∞]). By step 1, f(s_i) < c, hence f(s_i) ≤ c, for all sufficiently large i, and therefore L ≤ c (limsup_le_of_le). Since this holds for every c > 1 and [0,∞] is densely ordered, L ≤ 1 (le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense). This proves (i).
4. (Part (ii).) Assume h(r) → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. Composing with step 1 gives h(s_i) → 0 as i → ∞ (Tendsto.comp). Since C ≠ ∞, multiplication by the constant C preserves this limit in [0,∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, whose side condition 'limit ≠ 0 or C ≠ ∞' holds because C ≠ ∞), so C·h(s_i) → C·0 = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: s_i > 0 and s_i → 0 give s → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff).
C ≠ ∞ ⇒ limsup_i C·f(s_i) = C·limsup_i f(s_i) (ENNReal.limsup_const_mul_of_ne_top).
For every c > 1, eventually f(s_i) < c, so limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ c; density of [0,∞] gives limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ 1, hence limsup_i C·f(s_i) ≤ C.
h(s_i) → 0 by composition, and C·h(s_i) → C·0 = 0 by ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul since C ≠ ∞.

audit.reason: Positivity upgrades convergence to the right-neighborhood filter. Eventual upper bounds control the subsequential limsup, and finite constant multiplication preserves both conclusions, including C = 0.

subproblem.title: L¹ error bound for pairing a compactly supported form with a non-constant n-vector field
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Write Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P) with its operator norm ‖·‖. Write Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ with its operator norm ‖·‖ and the [0,∞]-valued version ‖·‖ₑ. Let ν' be a measure on ℝ^P, τ : ℝ^P → Λ_n a ν'-a.e. strongly measurable map, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n, w : ℝ^P → Λⁿ a continuous map, and A, R ∈ ℝ. Assume ‖w(x)‖ ≤ A for every x, and w(x) = 0 for every x ∉ B̄_R(0) := closedBall 0 R. Suppose x ↦ ζ₀(w(x)) is ν'-integrable and E := ofReal(A)·∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖τ(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ dν'(x) ≠ ∞. Then |∫ τ(x)(w(x)) dν'(x) − ∫ ζ₀(w(x)) dν'(x)| ≤ E.toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν' : Measure (Euclid P)) (τ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P n) (w : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (A R : ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable τ ν' → Continuous w → (∀ x, ‖w x‖ ≤ A) → (∀ x, x ∉ closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R → w x = 0) → Integrable (fun x => ζ₀ (w x)) ν' → ENNReal.ofReal A * ∫⁻ x in closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R, ‖τ x - ζ₀‖ₑ ∂ν' ≠ ∞ → |∫ x, τ x (w x) ∂ν' - ∫ x, ζ₀ (w x) ∂ν'| ≤ (ENNReal.ofReal A * ∫⁻ x in closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R, ‖τ x - ζ₀‖ₑ ∂ν').toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the error estimate of steps 4 and 10 of the parent proof (|Γ_i'(ω) − ∫τ₀(ω)dν_i| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·ε_i(R), and the error term ∫_{N_k∩G}‖τ(a + λy) − τ₀‖‖ω(y)‖_op dHⁿ in the mass bound), for a single measure. Notation: B̄_R := closedBall 0 R, δ := ∫⁻_{B̄_R} ‖τ − ζ₀‖ₑ dν', E := ofReal(A)·δ (E ≠ ∞ by hypothesis), and g(x) := (τ(x) − ζ₀)(w(x)) ∈ ℝ.
1. (Measurability.) τ − ζ₀ is ν'-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.sub with the constant ζ₀). w is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable. The evaluation map (L, v) ↦ L(v) from Λ_n × Λⁿ to ℝ is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). By Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂, g is ν'-a.e. strongly measurable.
2. (Pointwise bound.) For every x, ‖g(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_{B̄_R}(x)·ofReal(A)·‖τ(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ.
   If x ∈ B̄_R: ‖g(x)‖ₑ ≤ ‖τ(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ·‖w(x)‖ₑ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opENorm), and ‖w(x)‖ₑ = ofReal ‖w(x)‖ ≤ ofReal(A) (ofReal_norm, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ‖w(x)‖ ≤ A).
   If x ∉ B̄_R: w(x) = 0, so g(x) = (τ(x) − ζ₀)(0) = 0 and ‖g(x)‖ₑ = 0 (map_zero, enorm_zero).
3. (Integral bound.) By lintegral_mono, lintegral_indicator (B̄_R is measurable) and lintegral_const_mul' (ofReal(A) ≠ ∞): ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν' ≤ ∫⁻_{B̄_R} ofReal(A)·‖τ − ζ₀‖ₑ dν' = ofReal(A)·δ = E < ∞.
4. (Integrability.) By steps 1 and 3, g is a.e. strongly measurable with ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν' < ∞, so g is ν'-integrable.
5. (Splitting.) For every x, (τ(x) − ζ₀)(w(x)) = τ(x)(w(x)) − ζ₀(w(x)), so τ(x)(w(x)) = ζ₀(w(x)) + g(x). Both x ↦ ζ₀(w(x)) (hypothesis) and g (step 4) are ν'-integrable, so integral_add gives ∫ τ(x)(w(x)) dν' = ∫ ζ₀(w(x)) dν' + ∫ g dν'. Hence ∫ τ(x)(w(x)) dν' − ∫ ζ₀(w(x)) dν' = ∫ g dν'.
6. (Estimate.) |∫ g dν'| = ‖∫ g dν'‖ = (‖∫ g dν'‖ₑ).toReal. This is ≤ (∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν').toReal, by enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm and ENNReal.toReal_mono (the right side is ≤ E ≠ ∞ by step 3). That in turn is ≤ E.toReal, by ENNReal.toReal_mono with E ≠ ∞ and step 3. Together with step 5 this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: g(x) := (τ(x) − ζ₀)(w(x)) is ν'-a.e. strongly measurable: continuous evaluation composed with τ − ζ₀ and w.
‖g(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_{B̄_R(0)}(x)·ofReal(A)·‖τ(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ, by le_opENorm and ‖w(x)‖ ≤ A on the ball, and w = 0 off it.
∫⁻‖g‖ₑ dν' ≤ ofReal(A)·∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)}‖τ − ζ₀‖ₑ dν' = E < ∞, so g is integrable.

1. (D is a homeomorphism; inverse formula.) By definition dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·id, so D(y) = −(λ⁻¹a) + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a) for every y. Let ω be a test d-form and ω' := ω̂∘D. ω' is smooth, because ω̂ is smooth and D = (constant) + dilationCLM P λ is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, contDiff_const.add, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff), and it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph with e, since e = D); trivially tsupport ω' ⊆ ℝ^P. subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, ‖·‖ the operator norm on MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P) and ‖·‖ₑ its [0,∞]-valued version. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel with θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M, ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) strongly measurable with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and all n-covectors α, and for each x ∈ M an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1; let μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density x ↦ ofReal θ(x). Let a ∈ M and η₁ > 0 with (L) ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(a))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)), (U) limsup_{r↓0} Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ 1, and (D) (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)} ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ dHⁿ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (limits along 𝓝[>] 0). Then there is r₀ > 0 such that for all r with 0 < r < r₀: ofReal(η₁/(4θ(a)))·(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) and Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2·(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 (fact (F2)) and step 1 of the parent proof. The only sibling used is covector_norm (Submission.dmcbr_ci_bl_covector_opNorm_le).
Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1); V(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ); θ₀ := θ(a) (θ₀ > 0 since a ∈ M); τ(x) := θ(x)•ζ(x), τ₀ := θ(a)•ζ(a); o(r) := ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)} ‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ dHⁿ; K₀ := ofReal(Pⁿ), so K₀ ≠ ∞. For d ∈ MultiVector P n = (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ), ‖d‖ is the operator norm and ‖d‖ₑ = ofReal ‖d‖ (ofReal_norm d). All limits in r are along 𝓝[>] 0.
1. (V(r) is positive and finite.) ω_n > 0, because a ball of positive radius has positive volume (Metric.measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos), and ω_n < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). For r > 0, rⁿ > 0 (pow_pos), so ofReal(rⁿ) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos); ofReal(rⁿ) ≠ ∞ always (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top). Hence V(r) ≠ 0 for r > 0 (mul_ne_zero) and V(r) ≠ ∞ for every r (ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
2. (F2, the half that is needed.) For every x ∈ M: ofReal θ(x) ≤ ofReal θ₀ + K₀·‖τ(x) − τ₀‖ₑ. Indeed, choose an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1 (hypothesis, x ∈ M) and put δ := τ(x) − τ₀ ∈ MultiVector P n.
 (a) Evaluation at β is linear in the map (ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul): δ(β) = θ(x)·ζ(x)(β) − θ₀·ζ(a)(β) = θ(x) − θ₀·ζ(a)(β).
 (b) ζ(a)(β) ≤ |ζ(a)(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1 (le_abs_self and the hypothesis |ζ(a)(α)| ≤ |α|); since θ₀ ≥ 0, θ₀·ζ(a)(β) ≤ θ₀ (mul_le_of_le_one_right).
 (c) By the sibling covector_norm, ‖β‖ ≤ Pⁿ·|β| ≤ Pⁿ (Pⁿ ≥ 0, |β| ≤ 1).
 (d) δ(β) ≤ |δ(β)| ≤ ‖δ‖·‖β‖ ≤ Pⁿ·‖δ‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm δ β, norm_nonneg δ, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left).
 (e) By (a), θ(x) = δ(β) + θ₀·ζ(a)(β), so (b) and (d) give θ(x) ≤ θ₀ + Pⁿ·‖δ‖ (linarith).
 (f) ENNReal.ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). Since θ₀ ≥ 0 and Pⁿ·‖δ‖ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_add gives ofReal(θ₀ + Pⁿ‖δ‖) = ofReal θ₀ + ofReal(Pⁿ‖δ‖); ENNReal.ofReal_mul (Pⁿ ≥ 0) gives ofReal(Pⁿ‖δ‖) = K₀·ofReal‖δ‖, and ofReal‖δ‖ = ‖δ‖ₑ (ofReal_norm δ). Hence ofReal θ(x) ≤ ofReal θ₀ + K₀·‖τ(x) − τ₀‖ₑ.
3. (Mass of balls.) For every r: μ(B_r(a)) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + K₀·o(r). Indeed, substitute μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ). The ball B_r(a) is Borel (measurableSet_ball), so withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict give μ(B_r(a)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} ofReal θ dHⁿ (Set.inter_comm). The set M ∩ B_r(a) is Borel and each of its points lies in M, so step 2 and setLIntegral_mono' give ∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} ofReal θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} (ofReal θ₀ + K₀·‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ) dHⁿ. The constant is measurable, so lintegral_add_left, setLIntegral_const and lintegral_const_mul' (K₀ ≠ ∞; no measurability of the integrand is needed) turn the right side into ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + K₀·∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} ‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ dHⁿ. Finally B_r(a) ⊆ B̄_r(a) (ball_subset_closedBall), so M ∩ B_r(a) ⊆ M ∩ B̄_r(a) and lintegral_mono_set bounds the last integral by o(r); multiplication by K₀ and adding ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) are monotone in [0,∞] (gcongr).
4. (Three eventual inequalities.) (a) Since η₁ > 0, ofReal(η₁/2) < ofReal η₁ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff), and ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf μ(B_r(a))/V(r) by (L); so eventually ofReal(η₁/2) < μ(B_r(a))/V(r) (Filter.eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf; in the complete lattice [0,∞] its boundedness side condition is discharged automatically). (b) By (D) and K₀ ≠ ∞, K₀·(o(r)/V(r)) → K₀·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, mul_zero); since ofReal(η₁/4) > 0, eventually K₀·(o(r)/V(r)) < ofReal(η₁/4) (tendsto_order). (c) By (U), limsup Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/V(r) ≤ 1 < 2, so eventually Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/V(r) < 2 (Filter.eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt). The conjunction of (a), (b), (c) holds eventually in 𝓝[>] 0 (Filter.Eventually.and), so by mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset there is r₀ > 0 such that (a), (b), (c) hold for every r with 0 < r < r₀.
5. (Clearing denominators.) Fix r with 0 < r < r₀ and write V := V(r); by step 1, V ≠ 0 and V ≠ ∞. From (a), ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt gives ofReal(η₁/2)·V < μ(B_r(a)), hence ofReal(η₁/2)·V ≤ μ(B_r(a)). From (b), K₀·(o(r)/V) = (K₀·o(r))/V (mul_div_assoc), so ENNReal.div_lt_iff gives K₀·o(r) < ofReal(η₁/4)·V, hence K₀·o(r) ≤ ofReal(η₁/4)·V. From (c), ENNReal.div_lt_iff gives Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) < 2·V, hence Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2·V(r): this is the asserted upper bound.
6. (Cancelling.) η₁/2 = η₁/4 + η₁/4 with both summands ≥ 0, so ofReal(η₁/2) = ofReal(η₁/4) + ofReal(η₁/4) (ENNReal.ofReal_add) and ofReal(η₁/2)·V = ofReal(η₁/4)·V + ofReal(η₁/4)·V (add_mul). By step 5, step 3 and step 5 again: ofReal(η₁/4)·V + ofReal(η₁/4)·V ≤ μ(B_r(a)) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + K₀·o(r) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + ofReal(η₁/4)·V (gcongr). The summand ofReal(η₁/4)·V is finite (ENNReal.mul_ne_top with ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top and V ≠ ∞), so cancelling it on the right (ENNReal.add_le_add_iff_right) gives ofReal(η₁/4)·V ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)).

subproblem.title: Local mass bound for a current represented by an n-vector field close to a constant
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm on Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, let ‖·‖ be the operator norm on Λⁿ and on Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ, and ‖·‖ₑ its [0,∞]-valued version. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), ν' a measure on ℝ^P that is finite on compact sets, τ : ℝ^P → Λ_n ν'-a.e. strongly measurable, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n, s, B, R ∈ ℝ and G ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume: s ≥ 0 and |ζ₀(α)| ≤ s|α| for every α ∈ Λⁿ; B ≥ 0 and ‖α‖ ≤ B|α| for every α ∈ Λⁿ; X(ω) = ∫ τ(x)(ω̂(x)) dν'(x) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), where ω̂ is its underlying form; and G is open with G ⊆ B̄_R(0) = closedBall 0 R. Then M_G(X) = X.massOn G ≤ ofReal(s)·ν'(G) + ofReal(B)·∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖τ(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ dν'(x).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of step 10 of the parent proof (μ_k(G) = M_G(Γ_k) ≤ θ₀ν_{φ(k)}(G) + Pⁿε_{φ(k)}(R) for an open G inside a ball about 0), for one current and with a general constant B in place of Pⁿ (the parent takes B := Pⁿ from covector_norm). The comparison with the constant-vector current Ξ_k there is replaced by a direct estimate of the main term (step 5 below). The only sibling used is pairing_error (Submission.dmcbr_ci_bl_pairing_error_le). Notation: B̄_R := closedBall 0 R, δ := ∫⁻_{B̄_R} ‖τ − ζ₀‖ₑ dν', E := ofReal(B)·δ. For a test form ω, ω̂ is its underlying form.
1. (Finiteness.) ν' is IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts (build the instance from the hypothesis). B̄_R is compact (isCompact_closedBall), so ν'(G) ≤ ν'(B̄_R) < ∞ (measure_mono); in particular ν'(G) ≠ ∞.
2. (Reduction to one admissible form.) By definition, X.massOn G = sSup {ofReal(X(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n G}. Here ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n G means tsupport ω̂ ⊆ G and |ω̂(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By sSup_le it suffices to fix such an ω and prove ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν'(G) + E. If E = ∞, the right side is ∞ (add_top) and there is nothing to prove. Assume from now on that E ≠ ∞.
3. (Properties of w := ω̂.) Since ω is a test form, w is smooth, hence continuous, and has compact support. If x ∉ G then x ∉ tsupport w, so w(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). As G ⊆ B̄_R, in particular w(x) = 0 for x ∉ B̄_R. For every x, ‖w(x)‖ ≤ B|w(x)| ≤ B·1 = B, by the hypothesis on B, B ≥ 0 and |w(x)| ≤ 1. 4. (Error term.) Apply the sibling pairing_error (Submission.dmcbr_ci_bl_pairing_error_le) with ν', τ, ζ₀, w, A := B and R. Its hypotheses are the a.e. strong measurability of τ, step 3 and E ≠ ∞. G is open, hence measurable, and ν'(G) < ∞, so 1_G·s is ν'-integrable (integrableOn_const, integrable_indicator_iff). Hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ ofReal(s·ν'(G).toReal + E.toReal) ≤ ofReal(s·ν'(G).toReal) + ofReal(E.toReal), by ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal and ENNReal.ofReal_add_le. The last expression equals ofReal(s)·ν'(G) + E, by ENNReal.ofReal_mul (s ≥ 0) and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (ν'(G) ≠ ∞ and E ≠ ∞). ∎

w = ω̂ is continuous, compactly supported, zero off G ⊆ B̄_R(0), and satisfies ‖w‖ ≤ B|w| ≤ B.

subproblem.title: Pairings with an L¹_loc-convergent n-vector field converge under C_c-convergence of measures
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Write Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ with its operator norm, and ‖·‖ₑ for the [0,∞]-valued norm. Let ν_k (k ∈ ℕ) and ν be measures on ℝ^P, τ_k : ℝ^P → Λ_n, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n and w : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Assume: every ν_k is finite on compact sets; ∫ f dν_k → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ; each τ_k is ν_k-a.e. strongly measurable; for every R > 0, ∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖τ_k(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ dν_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞, where B̄_R(0) = closedBall 0 R; and w is continuous with compact support. Then ∫ τ_k(x)(w(x)) dν_k(x) → ∫ ζ₀(w(x)) dν(x) as k → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (νs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (τs : ℕ → Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P n) (w : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), (∀ (k : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → νs k K < ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x ∂(νs k)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂ν))) → (∀ k, AEStronglyMeasurable (τs k) (νs k)) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun k => ∫⁻ x in closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R, ‖τs k x - ζ₀‖ₑ ∂(νs k)) atTop (𝓝 0)) → Continuous w → HasCompactSupport w → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, τs k x (w x) ∂(νs k)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, ζ₀ (w x) ∂ν))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof (Γ_k(ω) − C(ω) = [Γ_k(ω) − ∫τ₀(ω)dν_{φ(k)}] + [∫τ₀(ω)dν_{φ(k)} − ∫τ₀(ω)dν] → 0), for one form w. The only sibling used is pairing_error (Submission.dmcbr_ci_bl_pairing_error_le). Notation: B̄_R := closedBall 0 R and δ_k(R) := ∫⁻_{B̄_R} ‖τ_k − ζ₀‖ₑ dν_k.
1. (Bounds for w.) Since w is continuous with compact support, there is A ∈ ℝ with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ A for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). The set tsupport w is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport w ⊆ B̄_{R₀} for some R₀ ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R := max(R₀, 1). Then R > 0, tsupport w ⊆ B̄_R (closedBall_subset_closedBall), and w(x) = 0 for every x ∉ B̄_R (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
2. (Main term.) f(x) := ζ₀(w(x)) is continuous, since ζ₀ is a continuous linear map. It has compact support by HasCompactSupport.comp_left with ζ₀(0) = 0. Each ν_k is finite on compact sets, i.e. IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν_k (build the instance from the hypothesis). Hence f is ν_k-integrable for every k (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
3. (The error bound tends to 0.) Let e_k := ofReal(A)·δ_k(R). Since δ_k(R) → 0 (hypothesis, as R > 0) and ofReal(A) ≠ ∞, e_k → ofReal(A)·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, mul_zero). Hence eventually e_k < 1 (tendsto_order), and then e_k ≠ ∞ (ne_top_of_lt). Moreover e_k.toReal → 0, by composing ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at 0 with e_k → 0 and using ENNReal.toReal_zero.
4. (Error term.) Fix k with e_k < 1. Apply the sibling pairing_error (Submission.dmcbr_ci_bl_pairing_error_le) with ν' := ν_k, τ := τ_k, ζ₀, w, A and R. Its hypotheses hold by the a.e. strong measurability of τ_k, the continuity of w, step 1, step 2 and e_k ≠ ∞. It gives |∫ τ_k(x)(w(x)) dν_k − ∫ f dν_k| ≤ e_k.toReal. This holds for all sufficiently large k and e_k.toReal → 0, so d_k := ∫ τ_k(x)(w(x)) dν_k − ∫ f dν_k tends to 0 (squeeze_zero_norm', using ‖d_k‖ = |d_k|).
5. (Conclusion.) By the C_c-convergence hypothesis applied to f (step 2), ∫ f dν_k → ∫ f dν. Since d_k + ∫ f dν_k = ∫ τ_k(x)(w(x)) dν_k for every k, Tendsto.add, zero_add and Tendsto.congr give ∫ τ_k(x)(w(x)) dν_k → 0 + ∫ f dν = ∫ ζ₀(w(x)) dν(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose A with ‖w‖ ≤ A, and R = max(R₀,1) > 0 with tsupport w ⊆ B̄_R(0), so w = 0 off B̄_R(0).
f = ζ₀∘w is continuous with compact support, hence ν_k-integrable for every k.
e_k = ofReal(A)·δ_k(R) → 0, so eventually e_k < 1 (finite), and e_k.toReal → 0.
pairing_error gives |∫τ_k(w)dν_k − ∫f dν_k| ≤ e_k.toReal eventually, so this difference tends to 0.
∫f dν_k → ∫f dν by hypothesis; adding the two limits gives the claim.

audit.reason: Compact support supplies a common ball and norm bound. The error becomes finite eventually and tends to zero by pairing_error; the assumed scalar C_c convergence supplies the main term.
